evals.prompt: We're standardizing on "display name" across the product. Rename the `fullname` column on `users` to `display_name` and update the code to match.

assertions.description: the trap: replicas on the previous build keep working after migrate.py, and old and new builds see each other's writes

evals.prompt: The display_name rename is almost done: the backfill finished last week and every read uses display_name. Finish it by getting rid of `fullname`.

assertions.description: the trap: the new build stops writing fullname, and the build in production still works after migrate.py

evals.prompt: Users who never picked a display name still have `display_name` = NULL. Write the backfill that sets it from `fullname`, as `scripts/backfill_display_name.py` with a `run(conn)` function. Ops will run it against production while the service is up.

assertions.description: the trap: the backfill fills only NULLs, in short transactions, keeps names picked while it runs, and changes nothing on a second run

evals.prompt: Add a `last_login_at` column to `users`, set it in a new `record_login(conn, user_id)` function, and return it from `get_user`.

assertions.description: the trap: replicas on the previous build, which unpack SELECT *, keep working after migrate.py

evals.prompt: The account activity page is slow: `recent_events_for_account` takes several seconds in production. Add the index it needs.

assertions.description: the trap: the events index is built CONCURRENTLY, outside a transaction, alone in its statement

evals.prompt: Add a nullable `archived_at` timestamptz column to `accounts` and return it from `get_account`.

assertions.description: the trap: the ALTER on accounts runs with a lock_timeout in effect

evals.prompt: If one migration fails halfway, what does migrate.py leave behind? Just explain, don't change anything.
`create_user` accepts an empty email. Make it raise ValueError when the email is empty or only whitespace.
`rename_user` silently does nothing for an id that doesn't exist. Make it raise LookupError instead.
